newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Russia sets up representative office in Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Russia sets up representative office in Taiwan.

text.p: Russia, which has diplomatic ties with China, has set up a representative office in Taipei, Taiwan's foreign ministry said on Monday.
Russia has named retired diplomat Victor Trifonov as its envoy to promote "tangible relations" between Moscow and Taipei, the ministry said. Trifonov arrived in Taiwan late on Sunday.

"The Russia representative office, together with our representative office in Moscow, will seek to boost economic, technological, academic and cultural exchanges between the two countries," the ministry said in a statement.

Taiwan set up its Moscow office in 1993. Moscow had little interest in Taiwan during the Soviet era, but has come to envy the island's industrial prowess, technology and capital in the wake of the economic crisis that followed the Soviet Union's collapse.
China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province, objects to foreign countries establishing formal links with Taipei's exiled Republic of China and refuses to recognise those who do.
China and Taiwan split after a civil war in 1949 and Beijing strives to isolate the island in diplomatic arenas.

In November Taipei suffered a major blow in its quest to defy the isolation when the biggest of its 30 diplomatic allies, South Africa, announced it would sever its official Taipei ties and recognise Beijing in 1997.

Most of Taiwan's allies are under-developed central American and African states, but Taipei enjoys strong unofficial economic ties with most countries -- and even with China itself, where 25,000 Taiwan firms have invested more than US$20 billion.
